title: Determinants of coercive measures using data from the IFuB statistical database
summary:
The project examines the circumstances under which involuntary hospitalisation and other coercive measures occur in psychiatric hospitals. These measures include, in particular, seclusion, mechanical restraint, and involuntary medication. While they may be necessary in acute crisis situations, they represent substantial restrictions on the rights of those affected and may have distressing consequences.

The study is based on pseudonymised routine data from the nine LVR psychiatric hospitals in the Rhineland region. Approximately 500,000 inpatient and day-patient treatment episodes from 2016 to 2025 will be analysed. The study will examine, among other aspects, how often and for how long coercive measures are used, the reasons for their use, and the clinical, social, and service-related factors associated with them. It will also consider differences between adult and child and adolescent psychiatric settings, as well as between different social groups.

The aim is to improve understanding of the factors associated with an increased risk of these measures. The findings are intended to support the further development of psychiatric care and, wherever possible, to prevent coercive measures or reduce their duration and frequency. All analyses will be conducted exclusively using pseudonymised data.

interventions.name: Retrospective secondary data analysis: Analysis of routinely collected clinical patient data from the statistical database of the LVR hospital group. 500,000 inpatient and day-treatment cases with mental disorders from 2016 to 2025, with the observation period extended over the course of the project

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All treatment episodes from the adult psychiatric and child and adolescent psychiatric hospitals within the LVR hospital network will be included. Initially, all episodes with a discharge date between 1 January 2016 and 31 December 2025 will be analysed. Over the course of the project, the analysis period will be progressively extended to include subsequent years.
Exclusion criteria:
An objection to the use of treatment data for research purposes may be made pursuant to Article 21 of the GDPR.
